For a plug-in backup, **the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a reasonable pick: its 2,073.6 Wh capacity is listed as enough for roughly a day of running a 100 W ceramic heat emitter through a thermostat, depending on how often the heater actually switches on. [See the product and runtime estimate](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage).

Before buying, check your heater’s wattage and make sure the station’s AC output can handle it. Runtime varies with room temperature, enclosure insulation, and thermostat cycling, so treat “about a day” as an estimate—not a guarantee. A low-wattage heat mat will generally last longer than a heat lamp. Insulating the enclosure can also help conserve warmth; keep the thermostat in control of any powered heater. [Petco’s outage-care guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage) discusses emergency warmth and backup options.
